page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores using an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or a GPU, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.sn2.xlarge sits primarily in the lower tiers for modern compute tasks. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, fall into the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, memory bandwidth read operations and database operations on Passmark are weak. However, the instance maintains average performance in write-heavy memory operations and Passmark CPU extended instructions. It also demonstrates average throughput for small-scale language model inference, specifically processing 446.56 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn2.xlarge offers a dedicated CPU allocation without hyperthreading, which ensures consistent resource availability. However, the older Intel Xeon architecture presents a performance-per-resource tradeoff, as it struggles with modern, highly parallelized workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and intensive text or image processing. The lack of bundled local storage means storage performance is bound to network-attached volumes, which may limit I/O-heavy applications.

This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads that require dedicated CPU cores but do not demand high-frequency compute or massive memory bandwidth. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, lightweight application servers, development environments, and small-scale machine learning inference tasks using compact models.
